newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-SOUTH KOREA FACE EARLY EXIT AFTER SHOCK DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH KOREA FACE EARLY EXIT AFTER SHOCK DEFEAT.

text.p: Football powerhouse South Korea faced an early exit from the Asian Cup after a surprise 2-0 defeat by Kuwait in a group A match on Tuesday.
Hosts the United Arab Emirates finished top of group A with seven points from three games and reached the quarter-finals with a 2-0 win over Indonesia.

A goal by striker Bashar Abdulaziz three minutes from time put Kuwait into second place in the table equal with South Korea on four points but ahead on goal difference. The tiny country thus earned the second automatic quarter-final berth.
Indonesia, fourth in the group with one point, are out of contention.
South Korea, one of the tournament's favourites, have to await the outcome of the final matches of the other two groups to see if they will make it to the the last eight.
They hope that their record of one win, one draw and one defeat will allow them through as one of the best two teams in third place in the roups.
Abdulaziz took a pass in midfield and beat the Korean defence for pace before slipping the ball under the advancing keeper to score the all important goal in the 87th.
Jassem Al-Houwaidi had broken the deadlock in the 60th minute when he reacted first to reach the ball after Korean keeper Kim Byung Ji tumbled a free kick.
South Korea's ace striker Hwang Sun Hong should have scored a minute before Abdulaziz hit the net, rising unchallenged to put a header wide.

"I don't think our players played to their full potential and ability," South Korean coach Park Jong Hwan said. "I am not going to put the blame on any particular player or players, our team just did not play as a team."
Kuwait's coach Milan Macala said: "I hope this is the begining of the Kuwaiti soccer show."
UAE players were well on top in their match against Indonesia, taking the lead in the 14th minute.

A long throw in to the Indonesian penalty area was first flicked on by Adel Ahmed and then Adnan al-Talyani to the far post where a sliding Hassan Ahmed thumped the ball into the goal from close range.
The UAE went two up in the 65th minute when Indonesian keeper Hendro fumbled a low cross by substitute Zuhair Bakhait and the ball fell to Talyani who hammered it in from 10 meters.
In the final Group B matches on Wednesday, Saudi Arabia play arch rivals Iran and Iraq takes on Thailand.

Saudi Arabia, beaten finalists in 1992, have already secured a quarter-final berth with victories over Thailand and Iraq. Thailand have to beat Iraq -- who have beaten Iran -- to have any chance of qualifying for the next round.
Defending champions Japan have booked a quarter-final berth from two victories in Group C.
